newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Britain stays attached to its border controls.
newsitem.headline: Britain stays attached to its border controls.

text.p: Britain's new Home Secretary Jack Straw reaffirmed on Monday that the new British Labour government was determined to maintain national control over its border, asylum and immigration policies.

At his first meeting with European Union partners since the Labour party won Britain's May 1 elections, he said that while it might make sense for a central European country like Germany to dispense with border controls, it did not for the British Isles.
"...I think that there's a high degree of understanding by our continental European partners," Straw told reporters after the meeting in Brussels.

As part of a treaty review, Britain's continental partners want an agreement to drop internal EU border controls. But Prime Minister Tony Blair stressed last week at his first meeting with EU leaders Britain's controls were there to stay.

"We are clear that the UK (United Kingdom) has to maintain its own border controls at ports of entry and control of the UK parliament over other matters which include immigration and asylum policy," Straw said on Monday.

Although the new Labour government has discarded many Conservative-era standpoints seen as nationalist and anti-European, it shares the unwillingness of its predecessor to give up sovereignty over borders and immigration policy.
Straw said that if Britain abandoned its border system, it could evolve into something similar to a "police state" where its citizens would have to carry personal identity cards. 261904 GMT may 97
